messages.content: What is the freezing point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure, provided in kilopascals (kPa) or atmospheres (atm). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The chemical name of the substance for which to calculate the boiling point, such as 'water' or 'ethanol'.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point, expressed in the unit specified by the 'unit' parameter. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the pressure value. Accepts either 'kPa' or 'atm'.

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the equilibrium melting/freezing temperature of pure water is essentially unchanged from its standard‑pressure value. Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid transition,

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}= \frac{T\,\Delta V}{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}},
\]

with \(T\simeq 273\;\text{K}\), \(\Delta V\simeq -1.6\times10^{-6}\;\text{m}^3\!\!/\text{mol}\) (ice is slightly less dense than liquid water) and \(\Delta H_{\text{fus}}\simeq 6.0\times10^{3}\;\text{J}\!\!/\text{mol}\), gives

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\approx -4.3\times10^{-8}\;\text{K}\!\!/\text{Pa}
          \;=\;-4.3\times10^{-3}\;\text{K}\!\!/\text{kPa}.
\]

A pressure drop of 10 kPa therefore shifts the melting point by only

\[
\Delta T \approx \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
           \approx (-4.3\times10^{-3}\;\text{K}/\text{kPa})(10\;\text{kPa})
           \approx -0.043\;\text{K},
\]

i.e. about –0.04 °C relative to the 0 °C at 1 atm. In practice this is within experimental uncertainty, so the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is effectively **0 °C** (≈273.15 K).
